summary: Kamembe Airport (KME/HRZA) is a regional airport serving southwestern Rwanda, located near the town of Kamembe in the Rusizi District, close to the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo. It functions as the primary gateway for travelers heading to Nyungwe Forest National Park, one of Africa's oldest rainforests. The airport has undergone upgrades to accommodate growing tourism to the region, supporting both domestic connectivity and regional flights.
faqs:
Q: What is Kamembe Airport used for?
A: It primarily serves tourists visiting Nyungwe Forest National Park and the Lake Kivu region, as well as regional travelers crossing into eastern DR Congo.

Q: How do you get from Kamembe Airport to Nyungwe Forest?
A: The drive from Kamembe Airport to Nyungwe Forest National Park takes roughly 1.5–2 hours by road, covering approximately 90 km along winding mountain routes.

Q: Is Kamembe an international airport?
A: It handles a small number of regional international flights, mainly from neighboring countries, but most international travelers connect through Kigali International Airport (KGL).

Q: When is the best time to fly into Kamembe?
A: The dry seasons (June–September and December–February) are most popular, offering clearer skies and better conditions for trekking in nearby Nyungwe Forest.
transport_tips: Pre-arrange a private transfer or taxi through your lodge, as on-demand transport options at the airport can be limited. Shared shuttle services to destinations along Lake Kivu and into Bujumbura (DR Congo) are available but should be booked in advance. The road from Kigali to Kamembe takes around 4–5 hours, so a short domestic flight saves significant travel time.
local_tip: Pack a light rain jacket regardless of season—the airport sits in a lush, misty highland region where afternoon showers are common even in drier months.
